name: England & Wales
params_note: params verified against LitCal general calendar 2027/2028 (epiphany=JAN6|SUNDAY_JAN2_JAN8; ascension=THURSDAY|SUNDAY; corpus_christi=THURSDAY|SUNDAY; eternal_high_priest=true|false). LitCal grade ints: 2 optional, 3 memorial, 4 feast, 5 feast of Lord, 6 solemnity. Epiphany is kept on 6 Jan but moves to the Sunday when it falls on Saturday or Monday (1984 rule); LitCal has no such option, so apply holyday_transfer after fetching. Eternal High Priest feast (Thursday after Pentecost, LitCal key JesusChristEternalHighPriest) is in the England calendar per Wikipedia; request eternal_high_priest=true.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_calendars_of_the_Roman_Rite (England table incl. Eternal High Priest; Walsingham memorial in Wales)

holy_days_transferred: Holydays of obligation (Liturgy Office, from Advent 2017): Sundays, Christmas, Epiphany (6 Jan), Ascension (Thursday), Sts Peter and Paul (29 Jun), Assumption (15 Aug), All Saints (1 Nov).

1984 Bishops' Conference rule: holydays falling on Saturday or Monday are transferred to the Sunday. Applies to Epiphany, StsPeterPaulAp, Assumption, AllSaints. Direction (nearest Sunday: Sat to next day, Mon to previous day) is the usual reading but the page does not spell it out - UNVERIFIED direction. App must apply this after fetching LitCal.
Ascension stays on Thursday (restored as holyday 2017); Corpus Christi on Sunday since 2006.
Immaculate Conception, Mary Mother of God, St Joseph are not on the Liturgy Office holyday list so they are not moved.

holyday_transfer.rule: if date is Saturday or Monday move to the nearest Sunday

Wales.note: Wales has its own national calendar (liturgyoffice.org/Calendar/National/Wales1.shtml). It does NOT list the England-only entries above (George, English Martyrs, Dunstan, Bede memorial, Augustine, Gregory feast, Becket feast, etc.). Wales-specific list below; shared feasts of the Patrons of Europe (C&M, Catherine, Benedict, Bridget, Edith Stein) are as in celebrations.
